name: Common Cold
description: A viral infection of the upper respiratory tract caused by rhinoviruses. Usually mild and self-limiting, lasting 7-10 days.
detailedDescription: The common cold is one of the most frequent illnesses, especially during colder months. It's highly contagious and spreads through droplets when infected people cough or sneeze. Over 200 different viruses can cause cold symptoms.
medications: Paracetamol/Acetaminophen for fever and pain relief
Throat lozenges with menthol or benzocaine
precautions: Avoid close contact with others for first 3 days
Wash hands frequently with soap for 20 seconds
Use tissues when sneezing/coughing and dispose immediately
dietRecommendations: Warm liquids (herbal tea, chicken soup, warm water with honey and lemon)
Citrus fruits for Vitamin C (oranges, lemons, grapefruits)
Ginger tea for throat relief and anti-inflammatory properties
Avoid dairy if mucus production increases
Light, easily digestible foods (toast, bananas, rice)
doctorConsultation: Usually not required for healthy adults. Consult doctor if symptoms persist beyond 10 days, fever above 101.5°F (38.6°C), difficulty breathing, severe headache, or if you have underlying health conditions.

name: Flu (Influenza)
description: A viral infection that attacks the respiratory system, more severe than common cold.
detailedDescription: Influenza is a contagious respiratory illness caused by influenza viruses. It can cause mild to severe illness and can lead to hospitalization in severe cases.
medications: Antiviral drugs (Tamiflu) if started within 48 hours
dietRecommendations: Plenty of fluids (water, herbal teas, broths)
doctorConsultation: Recommended, especially for high-risk groups (elderly, pregnant, chronic conditions). Seek immediate care for difficulty breathing, chest pain, or high fever.

name: Migraine
description: A neurological condition causing intense, throbbing headaches often accompanied by nausea and light sensitivity.
detailedDescription: Migraines are recurring headaches that can cause significant pain and disability. They often run in families and can be triggered by various factors.
dietRecommendations: Avoid trigger foods (chocolate, aged cheese, alcohol)
Regular meals to prevent low blood sugar
doctorConsultation: Recommended for proper diagnosis and treatment plan. Seek immediate care for sudden severe headache, headache with fever/stiff neck, or changes in vision.

name: Food Poisoning
description: Illness caused by consuming contaminated food or water containing harmful bacteria, viruses, or toxins.
detailedDescription: Food poisoning occurs when you eat contaminated food. Symptoms usually start within hours of eating contaminated food but can begin days or weeks later.
precautions: Stay hydrated with small, frequent sips
Rest and avoid solid foods initially
dietRecommendations: Clear fluids (water, clear broths, electrolyte solutions)
doctorConsultation: Consult doctor if severe dehydration, blood in stool, high fever (>101.5°F), or symptoms persist beyond 3 days. Seek immediate care for severe abdominal pain.

name: Allergic Reaction
description: Immune system reaction to allergens such as food, medications, pollen, or other substances.
detailedDescription: Allergic reactions occur when your immune system overreacts to a normally harmless substance. Reactions can range from mild to life-threatening.
doctorConsultation: Essential for proper allergy testing and management plan. Seek immediate emergency care for difficulty breathing, swelling of face/throat, or severe whole-body reaction.

name: Anxiety
description: Mental health condition characterized by excessive worry, fear, and physical symptoms that interfere with daily activities.
detailedDescription: Anxiety disorders are the most common mental health conditions. They involve more than temporary worry or fear and can worsen over time without treatment.
doctorConsultation: Highly recommended for proper diagnosis and treatment plan. Mental health professionals can provide therapy and medication management. Seek immediate help for panic attacks or suicidal thoughts.

name: Tension Headache
description: Most common type of headache, often caused by stress, poor posture, or muscle tension.
detailedDescription: Tension headaches feel like a tight band around your head. They're usually caused by muscle contractions in the head and neck region. Can be episodic or chronic.
medications: Muscle relaxants if prescribed by doctor
precautions: Apply heat or cold compress to head/neck for 15-20 minutes
Practice good posture, especially when working
Take regular breaks from screens (20-20-20 rule)
dietRecommendations: Avoid skipping meals - eat regular, balanced meals
Limit alcohol and excessive caffeine intake
Magnesium-rich foods (dark chocolate, nuts, leafy greens)
doctorConsultation: Usually not required for occasional headaches. Consult doctor if headaches are frequent (>2 per week), severe, sudden onset, or accompanied by fever, vision changes, or neurological symptoms.

name: Gastroenteritis (Stomach Flu)
description: Inflammation of the stomach and intestines, usually caused by viral or bacterial infection.
detailedDescription: Gastroenteritis is commonly called 'stomach flu' though it's not related to influenza. It's highly contagious and spreads through contaminated food, water, or contact with infected individuals.
precautions: Stay hydrated with small, frequent sips
Complete rest and avoid solid foods initially
dietRecommendations: Clear fluids (water, clear broths, electrolyte solutions)
BRAT diet when tolerated (Bananas, Rice, Applesauce, Toast)
Avoid dairy, fatty, spicy, and high-fiber foods
doctorConsultation: Consult doctor if severe dehydration, blood in stool, high fever (>101.5°F), symptoms persist beyond 3 days, or signs of severe dehydration (dizziness, dry mouth, little/no urination).

name: Sinusitis
description: Inflammation of the sinuses, often following a cold or due to allergies.
detailedDescription: Sinusitis occurs when the tissue lining the sinuses becomes inflamed, often due to infection, allergies, or structural problems. Can be acute or chronic.
dietRecommendations: Plenty of fluids to thin mucus
Avoid alcohol which can worsen swelling
doctorConsultation: Consult doctor if symptoms persist beyond 10 days, severe facial pain, high fever, vision changes, or if you have recurrent sinusitis.

name: Urinary Tract Infection (UTI)
description: Bacterial infection affecting any part of the urinary system, most commonly the bladder.
detailedDescription: UTIs are more common in women due to shorter urethra. Most are caused by E. coli bacteria. Can affect kidneys, bladder, or urethra.
dietRecommendations: Avoid caffeine, alcohol, and spicy foods
doctorConsultation: Essential for proper diagnosis and antibiotic treatment. Seek immediate care for kidney infection symptoms (back pain, high fever, nausea).
